33435507.t: Psalmi et odae cum catena, etc
33435507.b: Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library
g: Medieval and Renaissance Manuscripts in Beinecke Library
33435507.c: Manuscript on parchment, composed of two distinct parts, the first of which was added at a considerably later date to replace lost or damaged leaves at the beginning of the codex. Contains: 1) Michael Psellus, De Psalmorum titulis. 2) Cosmas Indicopleustes, Prologus in Psalmos. 3) Commentary on Psalms 1.1-10.2 [end Part I]; [begin Part II] Psalms 10.2-90. Folios 29 and 30 are misbound; they contain the text of Psalms 27.8-15 and 44.3-9. On f. 31r the text picks up where it ended on f. 28v, but portions are lost throughout the codex due to the placement of binding tape over the written space. 4) Odae ; In Greek. ; Script: Part I (ff. 1-28): written in a heavy round minuscule. Part II (ff. 29-331): written in a fine regular hand with an admixture of uncial forms. ; Crude headpiece (f. 11r), headings and small initials in red; some minor initials in gold. ; First leaf is rubbed and illegible in many places. ; Binding: Nineteenth century. Edges spattered with red. Half tan calf, blind- and gold-tooled with marbled paper sides.

33436177.t: Le Pelerinage de vie humaine, etc
33436177.b: Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library
g: Medieval and Renaissance Manuscripts in Beinecke Library
33436177.c: Manuscript on parchment (thick, poor quality; trimmed) of 1) Guillaume de Deguilleville, Le Pelerinage de vie humaine. 2) Guillaume de Deguilleville, three poems in Latin. 3) Poem added in a 15th-century hand, contrasting the life of a servant and a rich man. 4) Willem van Ruysbroeck, Itinerarium. 5) Summary of Aethicus Ister, Cosmographia III.31-39, on the land of Gog and Magog. 6) Jean Chapuis, Les sept articles de la fois; often attributed, as it is here, to Jean de Meun ; In Latin and French. ; Script: Composed of two distinct parts. Written by multiple scribes in cursive, with or without loops. ; Part I (ff. 1r-92v): illustrated with 79 column miniatures; two others on ff. 83v and 85r have been cut out. The miniatures are simple pen drawings, tinted pink, red, tan, purple, and blue, in pen-ruled frames, tinted in yellow; on ff. 18r and 22r with ivy leaves on hair-line stems at corners and centers. On f. 16v an unframed drawing of the carpenter's pax. 2-line initials throughout, red or blue with black or red penwork. First letter of each verse stroked in yellow. Proper names in red. ; Part II (ff. 93r-129r, 129v-141v) has two distinct formats. Between ff. 93r and 135r (art. 5), two 2-line initials, red, with simple brown penwork. Some capitals stroked in red or yellow. Between ff. 135v and 141r (art. 6), three crude tinted drawings, red, green and brown, in initials, either divided red and brown with red flourishes and dots, or red, with a scroll and a fish incorporated.

33447512.c: Manuscript, on paper, containing Sāniḥāt dumá al-qaṣr fī muṭāraḥāt banī al-ʻaṣr, or Correspondence, in prose and verse, with contemporary poets ; Copied in A.H. 1065 (A.D. 1655). ; In Arabic. ; Romanization supplied by cataloger. ; Incipit: "Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm. Allāhumma yā mujrī rakhā ṭibāʻ al-insān mustannatan fī ṭarāʼiq al-bayān, wa-mujzī raḥā ṣunnāʻ al-adhhān mufannanah bi-raqāʼiq al-iftinān, yā muṭliʻ sawāniḥ fikr al-afhām ṭulūʻ kunūz al-khabāyā, wa-mūdiʻ bawāriḥ fiqh al-aqlām khulaʻ rumūz al-mazāyā, yā mursil sarḥ al-khawāṭir tartaʻu fī riyāḍ al-maʻārif wa-al-ʻulūm, wa-munhil sawām al-ḍamāʼir takraʻu min ḥiyāḍ al-laṭāʼif wa-al-fuhūm ..." ; Script: Small flat naskhī, in red and black. ; Binding: In dark brown leather, Type III (without flap); cover embossed with central medallion. ; Decoration: Rubricated, text frame outlined in red. ; Colophon: "Tamma al-kitāb fī yawm al-Thulāthāʼ, sādis shahr Allāh al-muʻaẓẓam Ramaḍān, alladhī huwa min shuhūr sanat khams wa-sittīn wa-alf [10 July 1655], ʻalá yad rājī luṭf Allāh taʻālá al-khafī, ʻabduhu al-faqīr al-ḥaqīr Ramaḍān ibn Mūsá al-Muṭayyifī al-Ḥanafī, ghafar Allāh taʻālá dhunūbahu wa-satara fī al-dārayn ʻuyūbahu. 33449610.c: An account of a pilgrimage to the Holy Land, with outstanding illustrations, and with information on various eastern peoples met en route ; BEIN Zi +156 Copy 1: Variant: Last letter (e in "pere-") inverted in line 1 of fol. 4v. ; BEIN Zi +156 Copy 1: Rubricated throughout. Head- and tail-pieces hand-colored. Part of view of Jerusalem hand-colored. ; BEIN Zi +156 Copy 1: Imperfect: wanting plates with view of Venice, view of Modon, middle [?] portion of view of the Holy Land, and final blank leaf. Some leaves and plates appear to have been supplied from another copy. Some plates mutilated. Complete view of Holy Land supplied in negative photostat. ; BEIN Zi +156 Copy 1: Stamp: Ex Bibliotheca J. Richard D.M. ; BEIN Zi +156 Copy 1: Bound in quarter old stamped leather over wooden boards, with clasps; lined with four leaves from a vellum 14th c. manuscript on canon law; the clasp hooks are missing. ; BEIN Zi +156 Copy 2: Variant: Last letter (e in "pere-") inverted in line 1 of fol. 4v. ; BEIN Zi +156 Copy 2: Imperfect: Final blank leaf wanting. ; BEIN Zi +156 Copy 2: Bookplate: Frank Altschul. 33462266.t: Sermons from Palm Sunday to the sixth Sunday after Easter, etc
33462266.b: Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library
g: Medieval and Renaissance Manuscripts in Beinecke Library
33462266.c: Manuscript on paper and parchment. Copied by Pancratius Hales, regular canon in the convent of St. John the Evangelist in Waldhausen (Waldhusium, Regular Canons of St. Augustine) in Austria, between Linz and Sankt Polten ; In Latin and German. ; Script: Written by one hand in Gothica Semihybrida Currens; the spelling is deviant. The rubrics as far as they were executed are by an incompetent hand in the same type of script. ; Headings and marginal captions in red. Frequent red paragraph marks and underlining of text passages. Red plain initials (2-4 lines); from f. 66r onwards they are generally of a more refined type. ; Binding: Original undecorated white pigskin, with semicircular tabs (?) at both ends of the spine, over heavy leather boards. At the top of the front cover is the original shelfmark "D.II" (?); also a strip of parchment pasted onto the leather with the inscription: "Sermones a die Palmarum usque ad festum Penthecostis in papiro ***********. E.62" (s. XVI ). On the spine with four raised bands the handwritten inscription "SERMONES". The rear pastedown is a leaf in the same handwriting as the text in our manuscript, and probably belonging to it. Remnants of four leather ties at each cover, two at the outer edge and one in the middle of the upper and lower edge.

33465036.t: Summa philosophica quattor in partes distributa, 1639-1641
33465036.b: Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library
33465036.c: Manuscript on paper, in a single cursive hand, of a four part summa of seventeeth-century science and philosophy. The introduction discusses formal argumentation and syllogisms. The four formal parts draw heavily upon Aristotelian concepts as developed by Thomas Aquinas. Part One deals with logic and is illustrated by a Porphyrian Tree, while Part Two concerns physics, particularly the relation of soul and intellect, but also meteors, comets, weather and the oceans. Part Three is an exposition of an Aristotelian ethics, and Part Four, on metaphysics, is a brief compilation of orthodox dogma on the nature of God. The volume concludes with an unnumbered addition to Part Two on "celestial physics." Illustrated with over three dozen drawings and diagrams in colored inks and washes, this text centers on a comparison of the Ptolomaic, Copernican, and Tychonic systems with the system of Eustachius a Sancto Paulo (probably from his Summa philosophiæ quadripartita), and, finally, the " verum systema" of Aquinas. It also contains equinox and solstice charts, illustrated discussions of lunar phases, eclipses, and astrology ; Gabriel Thibauld was a theologian and member of the Order of Minims in mid-seventeenth century France. ; In Latin. ; Authorship from interior title pages: "A Reuerendo Patre Gabriele Thibauld dictata. In Conventu Minimorum Belliregardensi. Scribente Frate Seraphino Nicaeno, Philosphiæ Alumno." ; Three Illuminated and dated title pages, and other formal title pages,

33783332.t: Sharḥ Nukhbat al-fikr fī muṣṭalaḥ ahl al-athar : manuscript
a: Ibn Ḥajar al-ʻAsqalānī, Aḥmad ibn ʻAlī, 1372-1449
ابن حجر العسقلاني، أحمد بن علي، 1372-1449
33783332.b: Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library
33783332.c: "Treatise on the terminology of the Ḥadīth (sayings and deeds of the Prophet Muḥammad), by Aḥmad ibn ʻAlī ibn Ḥajar al-ʻAsqalāni (1372-1449), a leading Ḥadīth scholar and a prolific author, originally from ʻAsqalān (Palestine), born and died in Cairo, being a commentary on his own work Nukhbat al-fikar fī muṣṭalaḥ ahl al-athar. Copied on Wednesday, 18 Dhū al-Qaʻdah, 915 of the Hijrah (9 March, 1510). Name of copyist and place of copying not mentioned ; In Arabic. ; Title from folio 1a. ; Romanization supplied by cataloger. ; Incipit: "Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm. al-Ḥamdu lillāh alladhī lam yazal ʻāliman qadīran, ḥayyan qayyūman, samīʻan baṣīran. Wa-ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh waḥdahu lā sharīka la-hu, wa-ukabbiruhu takbīran, wa-ṣallá Allāh ʻalá Sayyidinā Muḥammad alladhī arsalahu ilá al-nās kāffatan bashīran wa-nadhīran, wa-ʻalá āl Muḥammad wa-ṣaḥbihi, wa-sallama taslīman kathīran. Ammā baʻd, fa-inna al-taṣānīf fī iṣṭilāḥ ahl al-Ḥadīth qad kathurat lil-aʼimmah fī al-qadīm wa-al-ḥadīth, fa-min awwal man ṣannafa fī dhālika al-Qāḍī Abū Muḥammad al-Rāmhurmuzī fī kitābih 'al-Muḥaddith al-fāḍil', lākinnahu lam yastawʻib ... fa-saʼalanī baʻḍ al-ikhwān an ulakhkhiṣa min dhālika al-muhimm, fa-lakhkhaṣtuhu fī awrāq laṭīfah sammaytuhā 'Nukhbat al-fikr fī muṣṭalaḥ ahl al-athar', ʻalá tartīb ibtakartuhu wa-sabīl intahajtuhu ... fa-raghiba ilayya thāniyan an aḍaʻa ʻalayhā sharḥan yaḥullu rumūzahā, wa-yaftaḥu kunūzahā, wa-yūḍiḥu mā khafiya ʻalá al-mubtadī min dhālika, fa-ajabtuhu ilá s

Resewn with heavy thread (fine cord?), three sewn-in chains linking the quires. Two strands of sewing cord cross over to the horizontal bars of a Z lacing, the diagonals of the lacing visible through the pastedowns of the inside of the flush wooden boards, the horizontal lacing protruding under the leather of the cover. The edges of the boards are concave at head and tail. The smooth, round spine is lined with a coarse, blue-green cloth extending almost to the center of the boards on the outside. The endbands which straddle the boards are laced through them. Covered in dark red, now brown, calf faintly blind-tooled with diamonds with crosses in circles at the intersections. 33796094.c: Manuscript on paper (sized, some deckle edges) of 1) Macer Floridus (Odo of Meung), De virtutibus herbarum. 2) Extracts from Marbode, De gemmarum, lapidumque pretiosorum formis, naturis, atque viribus: De chelidonio, De corallo, De allectorio. 3) Instructions for bloodletting. 4) Nine short recipes for various eye ailments. 5) Three short recipes for various eye ailments, in Italian (with some Latin interspersed). ; In Latin. ; Watermarks, in gutter: similar to Briquet Chapeau 3373. ; Script: Arts. 1-2 written in a small gothic script with humanistic features, above top line; arts. 3-5 in less formal scripts in larger module. ; Simple initials, 2-line, headings and numbering in art. 1, in red, except for ff. 37v-38r where initials are in black. 33834751.t: al-Durr al-laqīṭ min al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ. manuscript / Al-Juzʼ al-awwal wa-al-thānī
a: Ibn Maktūm, Aḥmad ibn ʻAbd al-Qādir, 1284-1348, author

33834751.b: Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library
33834751.c: Manuscript, on paper, containing Aḥmad ibn ʻAbd al-Qādir ibn Maktūm's al-Durr al-laqīṭ min al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, commentary on the Qurʼān, being an abridgment of al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ of Abū Ḥayyān ; In Arabic. ; Romanization supplied by cataloger. ; Incipit: "Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm. al-Ḥamdu lillāh alladhī anzala al-Qurʼān wa-jaʻalahu ḥujjatan, wa-awḍaḥa bi-hi lil-muʼminīn ilá al-ḥaqq maḥajjatan, wa-aẓhara bi-āyātihi nūran, wa-kānū min ẓulam al-ḍalāl fī lujjah, aḥmaduhu ḥamda man ittabaʻa nahjah, wa-rafaḍa al-bāṭila harajahu wa-marajah, wa-uṣallī ʻalá Nabīyihi Muḥammad al-mabʻūth bi-al-ḥujjah ... Ammā baʻd, fa-hādhā kitābun yashtamilu ʻalá dhikr mā fī kitāb Shaykhinā al-Ustādh al-ʻālim al-abraʻ al-ḥāfiẓ, shaykh al-nuḥāh, Athīr al-Dīn Abī Ḥayyān Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf ibn ʻAlī ibn Ḥayyān al-Nafazī al-Andalusī, nazīl al-Qāhirah ... fī tafsīr al-Qurʼān al-ʻAẓīm, al-Musammá bi-al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ ..." ; Script: Hasty naskhī, sparsely pointed, in red and black. ; Binding: In dark brown leather, Type II (with flap); cover and flap embossed with central medallion; covers heavily deteriorated. ; Decoration: Rubricated. ; Colophon of volume 1: "Kamula al-sifr al-awwal min Kitāb al-Durr al-laqīṭ min al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ. Wa-al-ḥamdu lillāh waḥdah. Wa-ṣallá Allāh ʻalá Sayyidinā Muḥammad, wa-ālihi wa-ṣaḥbih, wa-sallama taslīman. Katabahu Aḥmad ibn ʻAbd al-Qādir ibn Aḥmad ibn Maktūm ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Sulaym al-Qaysī al-Dimashqī, ghafara Allāh la-hu wa-li-wālidayhi wa-li-jamīʻ al-Muslimīn." ;

33836288.b: Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library
33836288.c: Manuscript, on paper, containing Maḥmūd ibn Muḥammad ibn Arslān ibn al-ʻAbbāsī's, al-Kāfī fī al-naẓm al-shāfī, code of Shafiʻi law; the last volume (volume 4) only. Wa-ṣallá Allāh ʻalá Sayyidinā Muḥammad wa-ālih. Kitāb al-Jināyāt. Bāb Taḥrīm al-qatl wa-man yajibu ʻalayhi al-qiṣāṣ. Qatl al-ādamī al-maʻṣūm ʻamdan bi-ghayr ḥaqq ḥarām, wa-al-aṣl fī taḥrīmihi al-Kitāb wa-al-Sunnah wa-al-ijmāʻ. Wa-ammā al-Sunnah fa-mā ruwiya ʻan ʻUthmān ibn ʻAffān anna al-Nabī, ṣallá Allāh ʻalayhi wa-sallam, qāla Lā yaḥillu damu imriʼin Muslim illā bi-iḥdá thalāth kufr baʻda īmān wa-zinā baʻda iḥṣān wa-qatlu nafsin bi-ghayri nafs ..." ; Script: Good naskhī. ; Binding: Modern library binding. ; Volumes 1, 2 and 3 wanting. ; On folio 1a: "al-Juzʼ al-rābiʻ min al-Kāfī fī al-naẓm al-shāfī, taʼlīf al-Shaykh al-Imām al-ʻAllāmah Muẓhir al-Dīn Abī Muḥammad Maḥmaūd ibn Abī al-ʻAbbās ibn Arslān al-Khuwārizmī al-Shāfiʻī, raḍiya Allāh ʻanhu wa-ʻan jamīʻ al-Muslimīn. Wa-al-ḥamdu lillāh Rabb al-ʻĀlamīn. Ḥasbunā Allāh wa-niʻma al-wakīl." ; Colophon: "Najaza al-juzʼ al-rābiʻ min al-Kāfī lil-Khuwāriz

33837364.b: Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library

33837364.c: Manuscript, on paper, in a single cursive hand, incomplete, containing copies of seven alchemical texts. 1) Antonius de Abbatia, "Incipit epistola prima...de transmutatione metallorum;" 2) Ramon Llull, "Tractatus de lapide philosophico;" 3) "Incipit liber fenicis," anonymous text concerning the transmutation of metals into gold; 4) anonymous text, in Italian, on the art of transmutation and on the "seconda quinta essentia;" 5) Ramon Llull, "Epistola Raymondi Lullii de accurtatione lapidis philosoforum," which contains a small illustration of distilling equipment; 6) Arnaldus of Villanova, "Incipit roseta nonella magister Arnald' d' villa nova;" 7) Ramon Llull, "Liber lucis mercuriorum: de compositione celestis," including an illustration of a distilling pot, alchemical recipes, and an alphabetical table of alchemical symbols. Several leaves missing from the end of this text ; In Latin and Italian. ; Accompanied by five sheets of notes in a twentieth-century hand. ; Script: Italic cursive. ; Binding: unbound. Seven signatures loosely sewn into an 18th century? paper wrapper.
